Over the past year, our group of experts - from the 'Digitalization in Energy' Task Force at United Nations Economic Commission for Europe | UNECE Sustainable Energy , which I co-chair together with Elizabeth Massey - has documented several case studies. 

These studies demonstrate that only through the practical application of previously researched theoretical concepts we can fully grasp both the benefits and limitations of digitalization in the energy sector.

The upcoming compendium presents five case studies from different geographies, each addressing unique challenges and opportunities within the digitalization of energy systems. By exploring these case studies, we aim to bridge the gap between theory and practice, showcasing both successful implementations and areas where improvements are needed.

1️⃣ The first case study (2023) - led by Dr Ana Trbovich with the support of Brian O Regan , Deval Pandya , Ioannis Vlachos, and Andrés Schöndube - addresses the challenge of distributed energy resources (DERs) integration to support #gridresilience , identifying key infrastructure requirements, assessing policy developments and deriving recommendations. In recent years, amid alarming geopolitical turmoil and a global pandemic, the inherent vulnerabilities of traditional energy sources have been starkly exposed to the developed world. 

For many developing nations, however, price volatility, supply shortages, and geopolitical dependencies are not temporary disruptions but enduring realities. 

The transition to a renewables-based energy system addresses many of those issues, moving energy dependencies from the global to the regional level and making most countries less susceptible to geopolitical disruptions. 

However, while energy security options will become more diverse, the energy system will also grow more complex, given the wide range of technologies and participants involved. 

As governments make substantial investments in infrastructure that is increasingly electrified, digitalised, and decentralised, it is essential that decision makers do not simply transpose outdated paradigms from the fossil fuel era onto these emerging systems.

IRENA's report, "Geopolitics of the Energy Transition: Energy Security", explores specific issues that should be systematically considered to guide national decision-making in navigating the existing and emergent challenges of a highly complex and integrated new energy system. 👇

Today, 600 million people in Africa still live without electricity. 

Studies have shown it is the best predictor of whether someone can escape poverty. The Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative has highlighted the correlation between lack of electricity access and poor health, unemployment, malnourishment, and more. 

To address this, I am honored to announce that The Rockefeller Foundation is supporting Mission 300 (M300), an initiative of the World Bank Group and African Development Bank (AfDB) to provide electricity access to 300 million Africans by 2030. 

Alongside the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP), the @Rockefeller Foundation is committing an initial $10 million for the Mission 300 TA Accelerator, which will boost the projects needed to double the current pace of electrification on the continent.

Former U.S. Government Head of the Power Africa initiative, @Andrew Herscowitz, is also on board to help steer the M300 effort. 

We believe that by identifying innovative solutions, working with additional partners, and measuring our progress in initiatives such as M300, we can help African leaders usher in a period of green, inclusive growth. #PoweringAfrica

The Many Facets of Energy Transition: From India to the World

While the world has made progress in renewable energy deployment, with over 40 per cent of the world's electricity generated from zero-carbon sources (Source: BloombergNEF), taking clean energy to the last mile remains a problem. 

However, India, which ranks fourth globally in renewable energy installed capacity, stands out as a pioneer in the Global South with its energy transition story.  It has facilitated access to clean cooking fuels for over 96 million women in merely three years; the rural electrification programme has brought electricity to over 28 million households in a span of two years. The rooftop solar programme launched this year, ‘PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana’, aims to bring the benefits of solar energy to 10 million households across rural and urban areas. 

What lessons can the world take from India’s citizen-centric, sustainable, clean energy transition? How does access to clean energy intersect with other factors such as health, gender, and economic progress?

Our session with @SEforALL at UNEnergy’s #SDG7 Action Forum delved into these questions. Swipe to see what our speakers said!

Uruguay’s transformation is nothing short of revolutionary. Within a decade, the country transitioned from relying on fossil fuels to generating 97% of its electricity from renewable sources! 🌱 Here's how they did it:

1️⃣ Innovative financing models: Power purchase agreements (PPAs) and feed-in tariffs helped attract investment, providing stability to renewable energy projects and leveraging private sector efficiency

2️⃣ Job creation and workforce adaptation: Uruguay’s renewable push created around 50,000 jobs, showcasing what a just transition looks like in practice

3️⃣ E-mobility and hydrogen: With the government’s Sustainable Mobility Trust and the development of a hydrogen economy, Uruguay is moving toward greener transportation and industrial sectors, aiming to decarbonize and boost exports

💬 Could Uruguay’s energy transformation be a blueprint for other nations? Let us know your thoughts!
